channel.title: The Unlikely Lab
channel.description: Research in machine learning, density estimation, anomaly detection, and collider physics.

item.title: Likelihood-Based Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in CMS Dijet Events
item.description: An unsupervised search for anomalous dijet events in CMS Open Data using neural spline flow density estimation, with an exhaustive validation and robustness study of the low-likelihood tail.

item.title: Mono-Z Dark Matter Search with Neural Spline Flows Using CMS Run 2015D Open Data
item.description: A likelihood-based study of mono-Z event kinematics using Neural Spline Flows and CMS Run 2015D Open Data, with separate studies of the electron and muon channels.

item.title: Hadronic Mono-Z Dark Matter Sensitivity with Flow Matching on CMS Open Data
item.description: A projected sensitivity study for hadronic mono-Z dark-matter production using conditional flow-matching continuous normalizing flows on CMS Run 2015D Open Data.

item.title: Why Do Anomalies Live in the Tails?
item.description: Why low probability can identify unusual observations — and why low likelihood does not automatically imply new physics.

item.title: Collider Events as Points in High-Dimensional Space
item.description: Each collision event is a vector of observables. Density estimation over that feature space connects machine learning directly to physics.

item.title: What Is Density Estimation?
item.description: Understanding probability density estimation and why learning a distribution can be useful for anomaly detection.

item.title: From Four-Vectors to Physical Observables
item.description: Four-momentum, transverse momentum, pseudorapidity, azimuthal angle, invariant mass, and missing transverse momentum.

item.title: Gradients, Hessians, Eigenvalues and Machine Learning
item.description: Gradients, Hessians, eigenvectors and eigenvalues — the differential geometry behind optimization and loss landscapes.

item.title: What Makes an Event Interesting?
item.description: A conceptual distinction between the different kinds of 'unusual' an event can be — and why only some of them matter for new physics.

item.title: Jacobians and Change of Variables
item.description: The mathematical foundation behind normalizing flows: how Jacobian determinants transport probability densities between coordinate systems.

item.title: Likelihood Is Not Probability
item.description: Probability, probability density, and likelihood are distinct concepts. Confusing them causes real problems in statistical analysis.

item.title: Neural Spline Flows
item.description: Rational quadratic splines, monotonicity, invertibility, and autoregressive conditioning in Neural Spline Flows.

item.title: Normalizing Flows from First Principles
item.description: From the change-of-variables formula to normalizing flows: invertible transformations, Jacobian determinants, and exact likelihood evaluation.
